The claim for compensation raised in this petition is in respect of fatal injuries alleged to have been sustained by the deceased Sh. Arun Mohan in a motor accident that took place on 03.12.2018,
at about 08.15 am, at Mehrauli Bus Terminal Stop, New Delhi, regarding which one FIR No.799/18,
under Sections 279/304-A IPC was registered at PS Mehrauli.

The vehicle involved in this case is a DTC bus bearing registration No. DL- 1PC-7047, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no. 1 (R-1), owned by respondent no. 2 (R-2) and insured with respondent no.3 (R-3).
2. As per record, the petitioners are wife, parents and younger unmarried sister of the deceased.
Succinctly put, facts of case are that on the above said date and time, the deceased Sh. Arun Mohan was waiting for a bus at Mehrauli Bus Terminal, New Delhi to go to his office at Gurgram, Haryana.

At about 08.15 am, when the DTC bus bearing registration No. DL-1PC-7047 came there, the deceased gave signal to the driver of the said bus by raising his hand to stop the bus but the respondent no. 1 while driving the bus in rash and negligent manner, without following the rules MACP No. 57/19 Srividya & Ors. Vs. Rajinder Kumar & Ors. Page No. 2 of 22 and in contravention of traffic rules, had hit the deceased from the left front side of the bus due to which the deceased sustained grievous injuries.

The finding on the aforesaid issues is recorded hereinafter in the succeeding paragraphs:
1. Whether the deceased Sh. Arun Mohan sustained fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 03.12.2018 at about 08.15 am, Mehrauli Bus Terminal Stop, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL-1PC-7047 being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3?

7.
Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
The first question that needs to be decided is whether the accident was caused by vehicle bearing registration No. DL-1PC-7047.

In order to prove the same, petitioners have examined Sh. Rajender Singh as PW-3 and has filed his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW-3/A wherein he has deposed that on the date of accident, he was waiting for a bus at DTC Bus Terminal, Mehrauli, New Delhi to go to his office.
He further deposed that the bus route no. 502 was standing ahead of the bus route no. 413 and there was sufficient gap between these two buses.

He further deposed that the third bus bearing registration No. DL-1PC-7047 of route no. 34 came from Terminal and a person who was standing between the gap of bus of route no. 502 and bus of route no. 413 along with some other public persons gave signal to the driver of bus of route no. 34 by raising his hand to stop the bus but the respondent no. 1 while driving the said bus in rash and negligent manner could not stop the bus and hit that person from the left front side of MACP No. 57/19 Srividya & Ors.

34.

Hence,
from the state of things as put on record, including the perusal of chargesheet (which is sufficient to prove rashness and negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle in view of the judgments discussed above), site plan, mechanical inspection report as well as testimony of witness, it stands proved on preponderance of probabilities that the aforesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing no. DL-1PC-7047 and the said vehicle at that time was being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no.
3, but there was rashness/negligence on the part of the deceased as well.
Therefore, 50% amount out of the awarded amount be deducted towards the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
Hence, this issue is decided accordingly.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

14. As rashness and negligence on part of driver of the offending vehicle/respondent no. 1 has been proved, the petitioners have become entitled to compensation for death of their family member in the said MACP No. 57/19 Srividya & Ors. Vs. Rajinder Kumar & Ors. Page No. 7 of 22 accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
